taskDescription: Arrange the steps of dietary protein digestion and absorption in the correct order, from the stomach to the enterocyte.
paragraphs: Gastric acid denatures dietary protein and converts pepsinogen to the active endopeptidase pepsin.
Enteropeptidase on the duodenal brush border converts pancreatic trypsinogen to active trypsin.
Trypsin activates the remaining pancreatic zymogens: chymotrypsinogen, proelastase and procarboxypeptidases.
Endopeptidases cleave internal peptide bonds, producing oligopeptides in the intestinal lumen.
Brush-border aminopeptidases and dipeptidases release free amino acids and small peptides.
Free amino acids enter enterocytes via sodium-dependent carriers; di- and tripeptides enter via the proton-coupled transporter PepT1.

overallFeedback.feedback: Protein digestion follows a strict proximal-to-distal order: acid and pepsin begin in the stomach, enteropeptidase triggers the pancreatic zymogen cascade in the duodenum, endo- then exopeptidases sequentially reduce proteins to absorbable fragments, and specific membrane carriers (sodium-dependent and PepT1) complete enterocyte uptake.
